chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ziyad al-Qandy, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), 'Teach me a supplication, for I have been afflicted with something' – and he had been imprisoned in Baghdad where he was accused of their wealth. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'Whenever you pray, prolong your prostration (sujood), then say: O One for whom there is no one, until your breath runs out. Then say: O One whom the frequency of supplication does not increase except in generosity and nobility, until your breath runs out. Then say: O Lord of the lords, You are, You are, You are the One from whom hope is cut off except for You. O Exalted, O Magnificent.'
Ziyad said, 'So I supplicated with it, and Allah relieved me and freed my way.'
ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam al-Hassan al-Awwan (AS) teach for relief from affliction?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual efficacy of prolonged sujood (prostration) as a means of divine relief, specifically noting the Imam’s instruction to recite titles emphasizing Allah’s absolute uniqueness ('Al-Ahad') and boundless generosity until breathless. Historically, this reflects the period of Imam al-Hassan al-Awwan’s confinement in Baghdad, where such supplications served as both spiritual solace and a testament to the Imam’s intercessory power for his followers. The practice underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical and spiritual intensity of prayer as a direct channel for resolving worldly afflictions.
